comparator.name: Bachelor Geneeskunde
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations and programme-specific appendices, corroborated by the current programme, study-programme and student-journey pages. The degree is 180 EC, distributed evenly over three years, with a 30-EC broadening minor in year 3. The programme integrates thematic blocks, projects, clinical-line education, professional-identity development and longitudinal learning lines. The OER appendices expressly state that EC cannot be assigned to individual competencies, tests or integrated blocks, but separately award 1 EC for sufficient longitudinal professionalism at the final examination. The reconstruction therefore preserves the authoritative 60/60/60 year structure, the separately fixed 30-EC minor and 1-EC professionalism component, rather than inventing credits for individual blocks or projects. The embedded Medical Science project is not treated as a separately credit-bearing independent thesis or capstone.

components.name: Year 1 integrated medical curriculum
components.note: Integrated blocks on a healthy start, growth and development, infection and immunity, and internal and external threats, alongside Medical Science and Sustainable Public Health projects, clinical-line education, professional identity and longitudinal learning lines.

components.name: Year 2 integrated medical curriculum
components.note: Integrated blocks on homeostasis, regulation, reproduction and gynaecology, and food intake and processing, alongside Health & Technology and Care Policy & Management projects, clinical-line education, professional identity and longitudinal learning lines.

components.name: Broadening minor
components.note: A 30-EC broadening minor completed in the first half of year 3 under the programme's minor rules.

components.name: Year 3 integrated medical curriculum
components.note: Integrated blocks on posture and movement, brain and senses, and ageing and the final phase of life, alongside clinical-line education and longitudinal learning lines. This component is represented as the 29 EC remaining in year 3 after the separately awarded 30-EC minor and 1-EC longitudinal professionalism component.

components.name: Longitudinal professionalism
components.note: The programme separately awards 1 EC at the final examination when longitudinal professional conduct is sufficient.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response builds from integrated biomedical and behavioural foundations into anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, cell biology, laboratory science, pathology, immunology, pharmacology, neuroscience, health psychology, epidemiology and research methods. It studies health and disease scientifically and socially but does not provide clinical placements or qualify a student to practise medicine.

alternatives.labelRationale: The route retains a substantial biomedical and behavioural core while adding programming, mathematics, data science, machine learning, medical imaging, neural networks, robotics, databases and AI ethics. The label states this interdisciplinary direction without claiming a dedicated biomedical-engineering or clinical-technology degree.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes dedicated epidemiology, anatomy, molecular cell biology, biochemistry, infection and immunity, neurobiology, abnormal psychology, medical and health psychology, sociology, psychodiagnostics and lifespan psychology. It adds programming, mathematical methods, introductory and advanced data science, machine learning, computer vision, databases, algorithms, linear algebra, robotics and AI ethics. Thirteen courses are shared and eleven differ, shifting the organising logic from broad biomedical and behavioural study to computation and emerging healthcare technology.

alternatives.concept: A population-health route connecting epidemiology, prevention and biopsychosocial health with quantitative and qualitative research, ethics, public economics, behavioural policy, organisational leadership, sociology, sustainability governance, global institutions and public communication.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the anatomy, cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory, pathology, immunology, mechanisms-of-disease, pharmacology, neurobiology, cognitive-neuroscience and psychodiagnostics sequence. It adds ethics, qualitative research, public and behavioural economics, organisational and diversity leadership, modern and contemporary sociology, sustainability governance, international-relations theory and persuasive communication. Eleven courses are shared with the closest match and six with the technology route. Its organising logic is prevention, populations, institutions and policy rather than biomedical mechanisms or technology development.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The first semester establishes biomedical, behavioural, epidemiological and professional foundations. Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes every selected life-science and biomedical course that formally requires it; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes all selected advanced cognition and psychology courses that require it. Research Methods & Statistics and the laboratory course precede the advanced statistical and evidence-synthesis work conceptually. The final four semesters progress through normal structure and function into pathology, immunity, treatment, higher cognition, health psychology, psychodiagnostics and advanced research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme's general medical, biomedical, patient-centred, clinical-reasoning, communication and scientific-research interests. Two further coherent directions remain. The programme's explicit Health & Technology project and interests in medical technology, evidence evaluation, AI and robotics support a health-technology, data and AI route. Its Sustainable Public Health and Care Policy & Management projects, together with prevention, population health, social context and leadership interests, support a public-health, policy and organisation route. Both are feasible and substantively distinct: the closest and technology routes share 13 courses, the closest and public-health routes share 11, and the technology and public-health routes share 6. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide an integrated foundation in normal human biology, health and disease; the comparator additionally embeds clinical skills, professional identity and broader medical blocks across the full year.
Human Physiology directly supports the comparator's second-year emphasis on homeostasis and regulation, but represents only one scientific part of its integrated clinical year.

Both study health and human functioning across later life, ageing and the final phase of life; the UCR course covers the whole lifespan and is not a substitute for the comparator's integrated clinical block.
The comparator reserves 30 EC for an approved broadening minor. UCR flexibility is distributed across the full 180-EC curriculum, so no single scheduled UCR course is asserted as an equivalent minor.

Both develop ethical reflection, feedback, responsibility and professional identity longitudinally; UCR addresses these across a first-year personal and professional development course rather than clinical conduct across a medical degree.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme is a regulated medical degree with integrated clinical reasoning, history-taking, physical examination, treatment planning, longitudinal clinical skills and patient-facing professional formation, followed by the medical master required for the Dutch physician pathway. UCR can assemble strong biomedical, life-science, behavioural, public-health, research and health-technology pathways, but it does not provide the continuous clinical curriculum, placements, supervised patient care or professional qualification of Medicine. These are academically related pathways, not substitutes for a qualifying medical degree.
